preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 50,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 500000 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and 'n' not in line])
preconditions.description: Each test case has a number of vertices n between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in [(int(stdin.readline()), [tuple(map(int, stdin.readline().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)])])
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly n-1 edges forming a tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n for n, edges in [(int(stdin.readline()), [tuple(map(int, stdin.readline().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)])] for v, u in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects vertices v and u where 1 ≤ v, u ≤ n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(colors) == n for n, colors in [(int(stdin.readline()), stdin.readline().strip()) for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: The color string has exactly n characters for each test case.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'WN' for c in colors) for colors in [stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: Each character in the color string is either 'W' (white) or 'N' (uncolored).

preconditions.expression: any(c == 'N' for c in colors) for colors in [stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: There is at least one uncolored vertex ('N') in each test case.

preconditions.expression: not any(all(c == 'W' for c in path) for path in get_all_paths(tree, n) if len(path) == 3)
preconditions.description: There is no existing path of three white vertices ('W') in the initial configuration.

postconditions.description: The output for each test case is either 'White', 'Draw', or 'Black'.

postconditions.expression: all(output == 'White' or output == 'Draw' or output == 'Black' for output in [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()])
postconditions.description: Each line of output corresponds to a test case and is one of the three possible outcomes.

postconditions.expression: all(optimally_wins_white(tree, colors) == (output == 'White') for tree, colors, output in zip([build_tree(n, edges) for n, edges in [(int(stdin.readline()), [tuple(map(int, stdin.readline().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)])]], [stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(T)], [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]))
postconditions.description: If the white player can force a win with optimal play, the output is 'White'.

postconditions.expression: all(optimally_wins_black(tree, colors) == (output == 'Black') for tree, colors, output in zip([build_tree(n, edges) for n, edges in [(int(stdin.readline()), [tuple(map(int, stdin.readline().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)])]], [stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(T)], [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]))
postconditions.description: If the black player can force a win with optimal play, the output is 'Black'.

postconditions.expression: all(output == 'Draw' for tree, colors, output in zip([build_tree(n, edges) for n, edges in [(int(stdin.readline()), [tuple(map(int, stdin.readline().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)])]], [stdin.readline().strip() for _ in range(T)], [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]) if not optimally_wins_white(tree, colors) and not optimally_wins_black(tree, colors))
postconditions.description: If neither player can force a win with optimal play, the output is 'Draw'.
